recipes.title: Pin, timer and bus: set them from this page, no code
recipes.outcome: Add the I/O you want with the plus: a pin (read it, drive it), a timer (toggle it), PWM (a frequency and duty), or the I2C bus (who answers, or read a register). Each row shows the line of C it stands for. Send, and the program on the board applies the list and reports back; the page checks a toggle and a PWM pin by sampling them through the debugger. A plugged-in BoosterPack from the list brings its own rows.
recipes.see: The pin you picked is lit on the board's drawing with its setup; the LED toggles at your times or dims at your duty; the bus answers with the addresses that acknowledged, or the bytes read.
recipes.before: Nothing to change if the board is as it came. The bus uses PA0 and PA1 with the board's own pull-ups (J9 and J10); put your I2C part on J1 pins 9 and 10, 3.3 V and GND.
